answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to stake scarce resources — bonded tokens or verifiable compute — before it can transact, so every fake identity costs real value. A single impostor drifts in like a zephyr across the tundra, harmless; but a thousand fakes need basalt-solid collateral behind each one, and the network slashes deposits when identities misbehave. Sybil resistance then comes from making identities expensive to mint and cheap to verify, so flooding the economy with clones stops paying.
